pie: kʷíd h₂usési h₁ḗdsi? mḗms h₃n̥gʷénh₁ h₂usési h₁ḗdmi pótnih₂ moy h₁íd pékʷeti. kʷíd túH h₁ḗdsi? mélit h₁ḗdmi wódr̥-kʷe píph₃oh₂. h₁íd h₂usési dlukú.
english: What do you eat at dawn? At dawn I eat meat with butter; my wife cooks it. And what do you eat? I eat honey, and I drink water. It is sweet at dawn!

pie: kʷís túH? h₁eǵóh₂ h₁suḱléwēs. nu kʷís túH? h₁eǵóh₂ h₂nr̥ménēs gʰóstis. gʷŕ̥Hte gʰóstey. méne ph₂téri h₁épi sddʰí ph₃dʰí-kʷe. deywṓs toy h₁wésuh₂ dh₃ih₁ént.
english: Who are you? I am Of-Good-Fame. And who are you? I am Man-Minded, a stranger. Welcome, guest! Sit beside my father and drink. May the gods give you good things!

pie: kʷíh₁ ḱód bʰéh₂mi? mélit dlukú. mélit dlukú. médʰu swéh₂dyos. nu médʰu péh₃oh₂.
english: How do I say this? The honey is sweet. The honey is sweet. And mead is very sweet! Then I shall drink mead.

pie: príHe moy kʷid wr̥h₁dʰí. ḱléwse. wĺ̥kʷos ḱóymom h₁n̥dó gʷémt. mélit widét h₁íd-kʷe h₂éḱh₃t. nu ḱwónes wĺ̥kʷom kʷḱént bʰéwgt-kʷe. HeHḱéwes ḱwónes.
english: Tell me something, friend! Listen! A wolf came into the village. He found honey and ate it up. Then the dogs saw the wolf, and he fled. Swift dogs!

pie: kʷíd gʰóstis? só h₂nḗr h₁yós nos ḱóymom gʷm̥yéti. h₁ím h₂életes priHós-kʷe nos bʰuHyéti. h₁eǵóh₂ toy gʰóstis? túH nos gʰóstis túH-kʷe nos lewbʰós.
english: What is a guest? He is a man who comes to our house. We feed him, and he becomes our friend. Am I your guest? You are our guest, and you are dear to us.

pie: awis akwabʰyams ā wawakat: kard agʰnutai mai widanti manum akwams agantam.
english: The sheep said to the horses: "My heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses."

pie: kʷíd deywóybʰos dedh₃té? h₁éymos ǵʰutóm médʰu sélpos-kʷe dedh₃més. deywṓs gʷr̥h₃ónti? h₁n̥gʷnís nos déh₃reh₂ gʷr̥h₃éti h₁íh₂-kʷe deywóns bʰéreti. h₁wésuh₂ wos h₁áyn̥t? suHnúns nos dʰugh₂térn̥s-kʷe h₁áyn̥t.
english: What do you give the gods? We give them poured mead and fat. Do the gods eat? Fire devours our gifts and carries them to the gods. Have they given you good things? They have given us sons and daughters.

pie: ḱód mélit dlukú? h₁íd swéh₂dyos. bʰréh₂tēr moy h₁íd dʰǵʰyés widét. h₁íd moy h₁opéye. h₁íd h₁áyso h₁íd-kʷe sélpesh₁ gʷr̥h₃é. h₁íd-ge sweh₂dú.
english: Is this honey sweet? It is very sweet. My brother found it yesterday. Give it to me! Take it, and eat it with butter. It is indeed sweet!

pie: h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m moy pérh₂esi? h₁íh₂m̥ toy pérh₂oh₂. kʷíd moy h₁opéyēsi? péḱu toy h₁opéyōh₂. péḱu? péḱu ne widmé. h₂r̥ǵn̥tóm moy dh₃dʰí ḱwónm̥-wē bʰére. nu toy h₁íd bʰérōh₂.
english: Will you sell me wool? I shall sell it to you. What will you give me? I shall give you money. Money? I do not know money. Give me silver, or bring a dog! Then I shall bring it to you.

pie: wéwke moy kʷíd dʰǵʰyés h₁édte? mḗms dʰǵʰyés h₁édme médʰu-kʷe ph₃mé. ph₂tr̥bʰós moy gʷéHyet sméyme-kʷe. swésōr toy smḗyt? smḗyt h₁ím-kʷe gʷr̥néHt.
english: Tell me: what did you eat yesterday? Yesterday we ate meat and drank mead. My father sang, and we laughed. Did your sister laugh? She laughed, and she praised him.

pie: kʷíd sh₂l̥bʰós? h₁éy sélesos gʷm̥sḱéti. gʷéwbʰos h₁ím dedh₃més. h₁ím lubʰyónti? h₁ím lubʰyónti h₁ím-kʷe liǵʰénti.
english: What is salt? It comes from the salt marsh. We give it to the cattle. Do they love it? They love it, and they lick it.

pie: kʷíd médʰu? médʰu mélit wódr̥-kʷe. h₁yós h₁íd píph₃eti só gʷéHyeti. nu moy médʰu dh₃dʰí gʷéHyōh₂-kʷe. ḱéywe ph₃dʰí séngʷʰe-kʷe.
english: What is mead? Mead is honey and water. Whoever drinks it, sings. Then give me mead, and I shall sing. Drink, dear one, and sing!

pie: nu moy príHe ḱóymom h₁éymi. mē h₁éys. h₁regʷesyéti. h₁idʰé l̥gʰdʰí. kʷíd h₁édte? mḗms h₃n̥gʷénh₁ h₁édmes. nu sédoh₂.
english: Friend, now I am going to my home. Do not go! It is getting dark. Lie down here. What are you eating? We are eating meat with butter. Then I will sit down.

pie: séh₂lm̥ h₃éngʷn̥ h₁n̥dó dʰedʰh₁té? h₁ím h₁n̥dó dʰedʰh₁més h₃éngʷn̥-kʷe swéh₂dt. méh₂tēr moy ḱód bʰéh₂ti sḗh₂l sélpesos priHós. nu moy h₁éy priHós. ḱéywe smḗysi.
english: Do you put salt into the butter? We put it in, and the butter becomes tasty. My mother says this: salt is the friend of butter. Then it is my friend! You are laughing, dear one!

pie: kʷíd ḱóymom h₂réydʰete? gʰósteyes n̥smé gʷm̥sḱónti. ḱóm h₁édomes píph₃ōmes-kʷe. kʷís gʷm̥sḱéti? bʰréh₂teres moy h₁éysōm-kʷe suHnéwes gʷm̥sḱónti. ḱóm gʷémoh₂. gʷm̥yé. gʰóstis nos h₁sdʰí.
english: Why are you making the house ready? Guests are coming to us. Let us eat and drink together! Who is coming? My brothers and their sons are coming. Let me come along! Come! Be our guest!

pie: kʷís h₁énom kʷékʷlom kʷért? ḱóymosyo nos dʰh₂bʰrós h₁ím kʷért. bʰréh₂tēr moy h₁ésmey misdʰóm médʰu déh₃t. kʷékʷlom moy kʷéreti? h₁ím préḱsdʰi. h₂r̥ǵn̥tóm lubʰyéti.
english: Who built that wagon? A craftsman of our village built it. My brother gave him a wage: mead. Will he build a wagon for me? Ask him! He loves silver.

pie: séngʷʰe moy. sweh₂dú médʰu keh₂rós-kʷe nos gʰóstis. deywṓs h₁ésmey h₁wésuh₂ dh₃ih₁ént. wékʷesh₂ toy dlukúh₂ méwdm̥-kʷe.
english: Sing for me! Sweet is the mead, and dear is the guest to us. May the gods give him good things! Your words are sweet, and I have become glad.

pie: kʷíd h₁wésus h₂nḗr gʰostéyey dédeh₃ti? h₁ésmey médʰu h₁opéyeti h₁ím-kʷe ph₂wéni h₁épi sodéyeti. kʷíd gʰóstis h₁opéyeti? sweh₂dúh₂ wékʷesh₂ wérh₁yeti. h₁yód linékʷti déh₃rom dédeh₃ti.
english: What does a good man give a guest? He gives him mead, and he seats him by the fire. What does the guest give? He says sweet words. When he leaves, he gives a gift.

pie: kʷíh₁ ḱód mléwHmi? séh₂lm̥ moy dh₃dʰí. séh₂lm̥ moy dh₃dʰí. tód wr̥h₁dʰí h₁ím-kʷe toy bʰérōnti.
english: How do I say this? Give me salt. Give me salt. Say it, and they will bring it to you.

pie: kʷíh₁ pékʷete? wódr̥ ph₂wéni h₁épi gʷʰr̥numés yéseti-kʷe. nu moy pótnih₂ sélpos h₁íd h₁n̥dó dʰédʰeh₁ti. h₁íd sweh₂dú? dʰugh₂téres moy h₁íd gʷr̥h₃ónti sméyn̥ti-kʷe.
english: How do you cook? We heat water over the fire, and it boils. Then my wife puts fat into it. Is it sweet? My daughters eat it, and they laugh.

pie: tód ḱeḱluwṓs h₂ówis h₂éǵrom ebʰuge(t).
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

pie: kʷíd gʰostíbʰos déh₃reh₂ dédeh₃si? h₁yós déh₃nom h₁áyto só déh₃nom h₁áyt. ph₂tḗr moy polh₁úh₂ déh₃ōr déh₃t polh₁éwes-kʷe priHṓs h₁ésmey h₁sénti. nu toy dóh₃r̥ déh₃oh₂. gʰóstey toy moy wékʷos sweh₂dú.
english: Why do you give gifts to guests? Whoever has received a gift gives a gift. My father gave many gifts, and he has many friends. Then I shall give you a gift. Your word is sweet to me, guest.

pie: kúdʰe h₂r̥ǵn̥tóm gʷm̥sḱéti? wiHrṓs h₁íd neh₂ubʰís wéǵʰonti. kʷíd h₁íh₁ kʷrinh₂té? kʷékʷlons kʷrinh₂més bʰréh₂tēr-kʷe moy swesréy médʰu kʷrinéh₂ti.
english: Where does silver come from? Men bring it in boats. What do you buy with it? We buy wagons, and my brother buys mead for my sister.

pie: suHnéwes moy ḱósmi dinóy ne h₁édn̥t. h₁íns h₁n̥dó wédʰe. pótn̥yeh₂su moy pékʷeti. túH nos h₁suménēs. dyḗws ph₂tḗr gʰóstins péh₂sti. ph₂syéh₁t te.
english: My sons did not eat today. Bring them inside! My wife is cooking. You are kindly to us. Father Sky protects guests. May he protect you!

pie: kʷíd dʰh₂bʰrós? dʰh₂bʰrós ph₂wéni h₁épi wr̥ǵyéti. h₂r̥ǵn̥tóm gʷʰr̥néwti h₃rēǵbʰós-kʷe déh₃reh₂ tḗtḱti. dʰh₂bʰrós toy ḱóymoy h₁ésti? méh₂tr̥s moy bʰréh₂tēr dʰh₂bʰrós.
english: What is a smith? A smith works by the fire. He heats silver, and he makes gifts for kings. Is there a smith in your village? My mother's brother is a smith.

pie: kʷís toy ḱā́m h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m déh₃t? swésōr moy h₁íh₂m̥ déh₃t. h₁íh₂ moy lewbʰéh₂. h₁íh₂ néweh₂ h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂. suHnúns moy woséyōh₂. suHnéwes toy gʷʰréh₁yōnti.
english: Who gave you this wool? My sister gave it. She is dear to me. It is new wool. I shall clothe my sons. Your sons will be warm.

pie: kʷís wos woséyeti? méh₂tēr moy n̥smé h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂h₁ woséyeti. h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m wésth₂er. h₁íh₂ wr̥ǵyéti gʷéHyeti-kʷe. h₁íh₂ nos priHéh₂.
english: Who clothes you? My mother clothes us with wool. You are wearing wool. She works, and she sings. She is dear to us.

pie: owis eḱwoi kʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses
